items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: INTERVIEWER: Is that Mr. Hardin or someone by the name? Yes, yes. You know him? Yes. [INTERVIEWEE] Well, I know he had it because he gave one to Jerry Heerman's.

ctx.x: close to that is that at the corner Canal and Rampart Street there used to be a small open truck, one of these light delivery trucks with an open wagon. And they had a couple of pieces of music in that, and a Negro standing in the back or sitting in the back singing. They used to give a little concert there on the street like that, but it wasn't like a street singer really. It wasn't Clarence Williams and Pirone trying to sell their music for us. No, I never saw them. The messenger at the Custom House when I was…
Well, I have seen the cover. Have you? Yes. Someone in Chicago has a copy of it, and I think I've seen your... Is that Mr. Hardin or someone by the name? Yes, yes. You know him? Yes.

Well, I know he had it because he gave one to Jerry Heerman's. I believe he did at least. Yes, that was 1909. It would have been 1908, but he said, Well, here, it's pretty near the end of the year. Let's get a very good, fresh date on it. We wait after the first of the year. So, he published that. How many tunes have you had published? That's all. That one? Did you renew it a few years ago? No, I didn't. See? That showed how little I was thinking of that until Jetty Roll came to town. You did? I wrote to the…
